crossRefs.note: I wrote to you in my letter to have no company with sexual sinners;
Levi made a great feast for him in his house. There was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining…
Their scribes and the Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax…
Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat, and celebrate;
When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”
Remain in that same house, eating and drinking the things they give, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Don’t go…
Whatever is sold in the butcher shop, eat, asking no question for the sake of conscience,
For we write no other things to you than what you read or even acknowledge, and I hope you will acknowledge to the end,
But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully…
Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are revealed to God, and I hope that we are revealed…

translations.web: But if one of those who don’t believe invites you to a meal, and you are inclined to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for the sake of conscience.
translations.bsb: If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.
translations.kjv: If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and ye be disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking ➔ no question for ➔ conscience sake.
translations.asv: If one of them that believe not biddeth you to a feast, and ye are disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience' sake.
